_readme: Single source of truth for the 'Check & explore' panels, the Methods tab, and SOURCES.md (generated by build_html.py; edit this file, not SOURCES.md). verified=true means the description was confirmed by a web check on `last_reviewed`; false means it comes from general knowledge and should be re-checked before relying on it. URLs are checked separately with `build_html.py --check-links`.

signals.name: Altmetric
signals.what: Tracks news, blog, policy and social mentions of DOIs — the best single “did anyone notice this paper” signal.
signals.use: Every Details Page API request has needed a key since Nov 10, 2025. Free for non-commercial research by application (review targets ~30 business days). The highest-leverage upgrade for the four editorial tabs.

signals.name: Crossref Event Data
signals.what: Was the free alternative to Altmetric: DOI mentions across blogs, social media, Wikipedia and more.
signals.use: Retired by Crossref (public API reported gone from April 2026); only a historical archive remains. Not usable for new papers.

signals.name: OpenAlex
signals.what: Open scholarly graph with citation counts, successor to Microsoft Academic Graph.
signals.use: Month-old preprints have essentially no citations, and fresh PsyArXiv DOIs 404'd at scout time. Use it for a 3–6 month retrospective: how did each edition's picks age?

signals.name: Semantic Scholar API
signals.what: Citation and “influential citation” counts covering papers and preprints.
signals.use: Same timing problem as OpenAlex; a second opinion on citations for the retrospective.

signals.name: Sciety
signals.what: eLife-built aggregator of community peer evaluations of preprints from dozens of review groups.
signals.use: Look up individual picks; an evaluation or curation statement is independent corroboration. PsyArXiv coverage not confirmed.

signals.name: PREreview
signals.what: Open, ORCID-signed preprint reviews with DOIs.
signals.use: Explicitly supports PsyArXiv, SocArXiv, OSF, medRxiv and bioRxiv. A published review of a pick is strong corroboration.

signals.name: OSF API
signals.what: Lists every PsyArXiv and SocArXiv preprint in a window.
signals.use: Gives completeness, not ranking: no view/download counters are exposed. Per-page counters (which exclude the authors' own views) render only in the browser. OSF's generalist server has paused new submissions since Aug 25, 2025; community servers such as PsyArXiv and SocArXiv are unaffected.

signals.name: Crossref REST API
signals.what: Lists every ChemRxiv preprint (DOI prefix 10.26434) and verifies authors/dates.
signals.use: Rate-limits under load (HTTP 429). Space requests out; the 7 unverified chemistry papers need exactly this.

directories.name: SPI-Hub preprint service browser
directories.what: Searchable directory of preprint servers with scope and policy details — the fastest way to find a field's servers.

directories.name: ASAPbio Preprint Resource Center
directories.what: Guides and server listings from the preprint-advocacy nonprofit ASAPbio.

directories.name: COS: community servers on OSF stay active
directories.what: Why OSF's generalist server paused submissions (Aug 2025) while PsyArXiv, SocArXiv and other community servers continue.

psychology.coverage: PsyArXiv carries a lot of psychology, but high-profile work often appears journal-first, clinical psychology and psychiatry often go to medRxiv, and cognitive neuroscience to bioRxiv.

corroborate.name: PREreview
corroborate.what: Open reviews of PsyArXiv preprints — a review of a pick is independent quality evidence.

corroborate.name: Sciety
corroborate.what: Aggregated community evaluations; check picks individually.

corroborate.name: BPS Research Digest
corroborate.what: British Psychological Society write-ups of notable new studies.

explore.name: medRxiv — Psychiatry & Clinical Psychology
explore.what: Where much clinical psychology preprints instead of PsyArXiv.

explore.name: bioRxiv — Neuroscience
explore.what: Cognitive and affective neuroscience preprints.

explore.name: Nature Human Behaviour
explore.what: Top general-audience behavioural science journal.

explore.name: Psychological Science
explore.what: APS flagship empirical journal.

sociology.coverage: SocArXiv posts only ~100 papers a month; most sociology goes straight to journals (ASR, AJS). Political science overlaps heavily — this edition's #1 sociology paper is an IR study.

corroborate.name: SocArXiv per-paper counters
corroborate.what: Each preprint page shows public view/download counters (contributors' own views excluded) — the basis of this tab's ranking; re-read them to fill the 35 unmeasured papers.

corroborate.name: PREreview
corroborate.what: Supports SocArXiv; check picks for open reviews.

corroborate.name: SocArXiv blog (SocOpen)
corroborate.what: Server news and aggregate submission counts (no per-paper rankings).

explore.name: APSA Preprints
explore.what: American Political Science Association's server (hosted by Cambridge) — natural partner if politics counts, or a candidate seventh tab.

explore.name: Sociological Science
explore.what: Fast, open-access general sociology journal.

explore.name: American Sociological Review
explore.what: ASA flagship journal.

explore.name: IZA Discussion Papers
explore.what: Labor, family and demography working papers that sociologists read.

economics.coverage: Economics runs on working papers, but SSRN's rankings are gone and fresh SSRN pages index slowly. RePEc indexes NBER, CEPR, IZA, the Fed series and SSRN-adjacent work, and still publishes measured download rankings.

corroborate.name: LogEc (RePEc)
corroborate.what: Real monthly download and abstract-view counts across IDEAS, EconPapers and NEP; CSV export via format=csv. Can restore a measured ranking to this tab.

corroborate.name: IDEAS rankings
corroborate.what: RePEc's ranking pages, including top items by recent downloads, refreshed early each month.

corroborate.name: NEP: New Economics Papers
corroborate.what: 90+ weekly field reports, each human-edited from the 500–1,000 new papers that week — independent curation per subfield.

explore.name: NBER Working Papers
explore.what: This tab's current candidate pool; nearly all cross-post to SSRN.

explore.name: CEPR Discussion Papers
explore.what: Europe's equivalent of the NBER series.

explore.name: Federal Reserve FEDS working papers
explore.what: Fed Board research series (macro, finance).

explore.name: VoxEU columns
explore.what: Researcher-written summaries — a column about a paper is a signal it matters.

philosophy.coverage: PhilArchive is the open-access archive inside PhilPapers, which indexes far more (new journal issues included). The real quality signal in philosophy is journal acceptance — most of this edition's picks already have one.

corroborate.name: Journal acceptance
corroborate.what: The venue shown on each card is refereed peer judgment; PhilPapers tracks journals' new and forthcoming issues.

corroborate.name: The Philosopher's Annual
corroborate.what: Selects the ten best articles of each year (45th edition, for 2025, announced Aug 2026) — a yearly check on the picks.

corroborate.name: Daily Nous
corroborate.what: Profession news; occasional reader threads on very good recent articles.

explore.name: PhilPapers
explore.what: Superset of PhilArchive; “Monitor current research” shows recent additions across journals.

explore.name: PhilArchive — Selected recent additions
explore.what: This tab's current pool (capped at 100 items, so only ~a week deep).

explore.name: SEP — What's New
explore.what: New and revised Stanford Encyclopedia entries.

explore.name: Philosophers' Imprint
explore.what: Leading open-access general philosophy journal.

cryptography.coverage: ePrint is the field's own preprint archive — the right source. Quality is decided at the top conferences, and a lot of security work posts only to arXiv cs.CR, which the beyond-arXiv premise excludes.

corroborate.name: IACR conferences
corroborate.what: CRYPTO, Eurocrypt, Asiacrypt and area conferences — later acceptance is the field's quality stamp.

corroborate.name: NIST PQC forum
corroborate.what: Where attacks on candidate schemes (MAYO, SNOVA, Falcon, ML-KEM) get discussed and vetted.

corroborate.name: IACR news feed
corroborate.what: Reposts new ePrint papers automatically (ePrint Report channel), so a listing is not an endorsement — useful only to see what's new.

corroborate.name: IACR Communications in Cryptology
corroborate.what: IACR's diamond open-access journal; acceptance there corroborates an ePrint paper.

explore.name: ePrint RSS feeds
explore.what: Publication-date-ordered feeds — the easiest way to enumerate a window.

explore.name: arXiv cs.CR
explore.what: Security and privacy preprints that skip ePrint (outside this digest's premise, but where much applied security lands).

explore.name: USENIX Security
explore.what: Top systems-security venue; accepted-paper lists corroborate applied attacks.

explore.name: ACM CCS
explore.what: Top-tier security conference.

chemistry.coverage: Most top chemistry goes straight to journals (JACS, Angewandte, Nature Chemistry) and many groups never preprint. ChemRxiv shows a slice; editorial highlight services are a better guide to what mattered.

corroborate.name: C&EN
corroborate.what: ACS news magazine; covers notable new results, including preprints.

corroborate.name: Chemistry World
corroborate.what: RSC news magazine; research news coverage of notable papers.

corroborate.name: Synfacts
corroborate.what: Monthly expert-selected highlights of new synthesis results with commentary.

corroborate.name: ChemRxiv per-paper counts
corroborate.what: Each article page shows views/downloads to human readers (bots get 403); a slow manual pass can test the 20 picks.

explore.name: JACS — Just Accepted / ASAP
explore.what: Newest JACS papers, the field's flagship.

explore.name: Angewandte Chemie
explore.what: Leading European general chemistry journal.

explore.name: Nature Chemistry
explore.what: High-impact general chemistry journal.

roadmap.title: Economics: rank with LogEc
roadmap.detail: Pull candidates from RePEc (NBER, CEPR, IZA, Fed series) and rank by LogEc downloads. Restores a measured ranking to the tab SSRN broke.

roadmap.title: Apply for an Altmetric research key
roadmap.detail: Free for non-commercial research; ~30 business days. Adds an attention score to every pick in every tab.

roadmap.title: Keep the corroboration pass weekly
roadmap.detail: First pass done Oct 18, 2026 (evidence lines on each card, Notable elsewhere lists). Repeat it each week and re-check the editions' picks for new coverage, venue acceptances and corrections.

roadmap.title: Filter by first-posted date
roadmap.detail: OSF counts a new version as a new posting; 8 psychology and 2 sociology picks in the first edition were revisions of older preprints. Enumerate by each preprint's first version date.

roadmap.title: Fill first-edition gaps
roadmap.detail: Verify the 7 ChemRxiv authors via Crossref, retry SSRN/NBER candidates, measure the 35 unmeasured SocArXiv papers.

roadmap.title: Decide on politics
roadmap.detail: Either a seventh tab from APSA Preprints or fold political science into Sociology.

roadmap.title: Retrospective at 3–6 months
roadmap.detail: Re-score each edition's picks with OpenAlex / Semantic Scholar citations and publish how the editorial picks aged.
